subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: What should strict-mode sanitization do when a user-delivery payload contains an unclosed `<think>` opener and a `<final>` body whose tags are stripped before the thinking fallback runs?
rationale: This choice controls whether OpenClaw may recover malformed answers or must fail closed to avoid exposing hidden reasoning, and the right default is a security/product boundary decision rather than a safe autonomous patch.

options.title: Define shared safe fallback
options.body: Adopt a shared sanitizer or stream-parser rule that preserves only a confidently identified final answer and otherwise suppresses unclosed reasoning, then cover WhatsApp and Telegram delivery paths.

options.title: Fail closed on unclosed thinking
options.body: Always drop text after an unclosed thinking opener in strict delivery paths, accepting possible empty replies to minimize hidden-reasoning exposure.

options.title: Use channel-specific splitters
options.body: Add WhatsApp-style stream coordinators per channel, accepting duplicated policy and drift risk while leaving the shared fallback mostly unchanged.

recommendation.title: Define shared safe fallback
recommendation.body: Adopt a shared sanitizer or stream-parser rule that preserves only a confidently identified final answer and otherwise suppresses unclosed reasoning, then cover WhatsApp and Telegram delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history for the current strict fallback and final-tag behavior is in shared sanitizer commits authored by this owner candidate.
